workload: Qwen3.5-0.8B, RTX 4060 Laptop SM89, vLLM fp8_per_block backbone, Marlin W4 full-vocabulary recall plus exact BF16 top-128 rerank, batch/concurrency 1, six natural prompts, 64 greedy tokens
interpretation: Marlin makes the two-row vocabulary scan cheap enough that lm-head weight traffic is shared, but this local kernel win does not amortize the MTP proposer, target verification, rejection handling, and extra host/runtime work.
The M=2 target path also changes upstream floating-point reduction behavior, so exact BF16 shortlist reranking alone cannot guarantee the same greedy token stream as M=1.
A longer qualification run is unnecessary because the screen misses both the performance and token-identity promotion gates.
decision: Keep the Marlin W4 shortlist/rerank candidate for ordinary batch-1 greedy decoding; close MTP-1 for this hardware/model/runtime point.
